annotation.title_clean: Ethical Implications of Stereotyping Robots in Public Spaces
annotation.title_en: Ethical Implications of Stereotyping Robots in Public Spaces
annotation.venue: Frontiers in Artificial Intelligence and Applications, Vol. 397: Social Robots with AI (IOS Press)
annotation.summary_en: Conference paper examining the ethics of anthropomorphic social robots that stereotypically represent social groups, using a fictional wheelchair robot representing disabled persons in public spaces. It weighs awareness-raising and minority representation against the risk of dehumanization, aiming to raise awareness of stereotypical design rather than settle the question.
key_provisions_or_claims: Stereotypical robot design can make implicit stereotypes explicit and raise awareness.
Robots can represent underrepresented groups and draw attention to minorities.
Robot representation of a social group may be illegitimate or dehumanizing.
Uses a fictional wheelchair robot case study in public spaces.
Aims to raise awareness, not to prescribe whether robots should represent groups.
